title: Introduction
text: I'm You Deserve a win and this is my week on Mycroft. I built a checker and it told me a defect affected 4% of the repository. That number was wrong and the thing that caught it was a second number that came out at 200%. Last episode I made the conformance checker actually open the step scripts. This week goes one layer up. title: The Command Every Recipe Documents
text: Reader to run a command called snickerdoodle. That command had never existed. The instruction was written 1,444 times across 97 recipes and nobody could run it. Three questions for any percentage in any report. One, what is the denominator? Name the population out loud. Two, could every item in it actually have been found or are some of them sitting in the denominator as silent passes? Three, is the share one defect or many?

title: Three Questions for Any Percentage
text: Because a finding in 97% of things that share a template is one defect, not 94. The ask was simple. Stop finding these one at a time by failing on them and measure how widespread they are without running anything. Here is what it found. 97 recipes, 616 findings. 94 of the 97 named step scripts that do not exist on disk and the number that matters for what comes next, zero recipes came back clean.

title: What the Check Found
text: Now the denominator. Four recipes advertise a flag that no script implements. Score that against all 97 and you get 4% which reads as rare. But 93 of those 97 have no scripts on disk at all. They could never have produced this finding. They were sitting in the denominator as silent passes. Second attempt, score it against recipes with no missing scripts. That is two, four over two, 200%. The right denominator is recipes with at least one script to compare four, four over four, 100%, not rare, universal.

title: The Same Finding, Three Denominators
text: The checker says this out loud in its own source. The comment records why the obvious denominator is wrong. Scoring the findings out of all 97 reports them as rare when they are near universal among the recipes where they are measurable at all. Question three and it changes what you do on Monday. 94 recipes name scripts that do not exist. That is not 94 defects. title: One Defect or Ninety-Four?
text: An afternoon and fixing it there closes it everywhere. The series rule is to recount rather than trust the commit message, so I ran the committed checker myself. 97 recipes, 616 findings, 94 of 97, four of four at 100%. Every figure reproduces exactly. title: The Recount
text: Snickerdoodle contract. Both numbers were right. They were counting different things. The other commit built the command. It was extracted, not invented. The spec was already written in every recipe. Gate decisions now refuse an approval when the gate's own test fails. Refuse any decision without a note and require a named human. Approving anything that touches live action takes a second deliberate flag. And one bug worth the whole commit. Gate tests are POSIX shell, but on Windows, they were running under the wrong shell. title: The Command It Built
text: That actually passes. That would have been written down as real evidence. Your turn. Find a percentage in your own dashboard and ask what is in its denominator. Then ask how many of those could actually have failed. If something cannot produce the finding, it is not a pass. It is not a measurement at all. 200%.
